question: Which Supreme Court of India judgment, and in which year, read down Section 377 of the IPC to decriminalise consensual same-sex conduct between adults?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NALSA v. Union of India (2014) is a landmark judgment, but it concerned the rights of transgender persons — recognition as the 'third gender', rights to self-identification, and entitlement to reservations. Section 377 decriminalisation came later.

answers.text: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, 2018

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018), a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India unanimously read down Section 377 IPC to decriminalise consensual sexual conduct between adults in private, while retaining the provision for non-consensual acts.

Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013) actually reinstated Section 377 by reversing the Delhi High Court's 2009 Naz Foundation judgment. It was this reversal that was subsequently overturned by Navtej Singh Johar in 2018.

answers.text: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Puttaswamy judgment (2017) established the right to privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21, and its reasoning about sexual orientation being an inherent aspect of identity helped pave the way for Navtej Singh Johar — but it was not the Section 377 decriminalisation judgment itself.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the 'Governing Principles — Legal Framework' section. The three key cases are NALSA 2014 (transgender recognition), Puttaswamy 2017 (right to privacy), and Navtej Singh Johar 2018 (Section 377 read down). Each has a distinct holding.

Correct. Knowing the precise holding of each landmark case — NALSA 2014 (transgender rights), Navtej Singh Johar 2018 (Section 377), Puttaswamy 2017 (privacy) — is essential for accurate medicolegal counselling of LGBTQA+ patients.
